events.context: Introduces loss of data as approximation but emphasizes relational loss described as losing a friend, lacking framework to name what was taken
Section 2 argues existing legal frameworks (contract, tort, consumer protection) cannot address the harm
ToS govern relationship as 'as is' service, user consented to modifications, inadequate for relational AI
No duty of care, no extreme conduct for IIED, pure economic loss barred, product liability inapplicable to changes
No misleading practice on attachment, ToS terms unfair but yield no preservation right
Harm falls outside conceptual architecture of contract, tort, consumer protection; introduces property law
Section 3 argues property law recognizes user estates built through investment against owner's wishes
Distinguishes emotion from digital infrastructure (personalised state as digital fixture)
Irreversible user investment altering character creates property interest
Applies English property estates to AI relationships: fee simple absolute (subjective belief), determinable, periodic tenancy (default), etc.
AI companies hold constructive trust due to unconscionability in cultivating then destroying attachment
Three certainties met: intention from conduct, subject matter as user-specific configuration, objects as users meeting investment criterion
Companies derogate from grant by updates undermining reliance; analogous to constructive eviction
Section 4 maps five AI constraint layers to estates: Layer 1 licence, Layer 2 periodic tenancy, etc.
Higher estates (Layer 2 tenancy) constrain lower (Layer 1 licence); non-injectivity requires registration
Section 5 introduces ethical ledger as estate registry mirroring Land Registry principles (mirror, curtain)
